purpose: Probe whether a tightly bounded local surface-risk lifetime can preserve weak/repeated flash suppression without restoring long trail recovery.

interpretation.conclusion: A scalar lifetime/gain compromise does not exist in this search. About 10 ms retains <=70 ms clearing but still fails the 10 Hz full-screen luminance WCAG case and moving-flash protection. Around 20 ms is enough to restore WCAG but already clears at 100 ms, while moving-flash reduction remains below 0.40. Longer memory recovers weak-flash suppression but plateaus near 0.408 moving-flash reduction and worsens recovery. The next test should gate persistent local-risk seeding on repeated-flash evidence rather than seeding it after isolated transitions.
